Subject: AuroraFin SIG - Access controls evidence needed

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the initial SIG submission earlier this week. Our compliance review picked up a few gaps under Access Controls we need clarified for our SOC 2/SIG audit:

1) SSO/SAML: Could you confirm the entityID and the SAML metadata URL for Redwood's hosted IdP integration? We also need an exported metadata file.
2) SCIM/provisioning: Please provide a recent provisioning log (CSV) showing create/update/deactivate events for the last 30 days for a sample tenant.
3) RBAC & least privilege: We need the role mapping spreadsheet and a short blurb on how least-privilege is enforced when new roles are created.
4) MFA: Is MFA enforced for all interactive admin accounts and do you have a screenshot of the enforcement policy in the Console?

If you can get these items to us by EOD Wednesday 6/18 that would keep us on schedule. Feel free to include any notes on contractor/third-party deprovisioning.

Thanks,
Jamie Park
Security PM, AuroraFin

Jamie —

Appreciate the clear list. Sharing the requested artifacts and short clarifications below; attaching the files for your audit pack.

1) SSO/SAML
- entityID: https://accounts.redwood.ai/saml/metadata
- Metadata file attached: saml-metadata.xml
- Note: We support SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows; metadata includes assertionConsumerService endpoints and signing certs.

2) SCIM/provisioning
- Provisioning log (sample tenant): attached scim-provisioning-logs-20250615.csv (events include create, update, deactivate with timestamps and actor).
- We perform immediate push provisioning and include SCIM delta logs in the private tenant audit bucket.

3) RBAC & least-privilege
- Role mapping workbook attached: rbac-role-mapping-202506.xlsx
- Short process: new roles are defined in the internal roles repo (PR-based workflow). Role owners must provide a justification and an attestation of minimal permissions; we run an automated static analysis that flags permissions that are broader than necessary and require reviewer sign-off. See sheet "Process-Notes" in the workbook.

4) MFA enforcement
- MFA is enforced for all interactive accounts with admin privileges and for any user accessing the Console from an unmanaged device. Screenshot attached: mfa-policy-screenshot.png

Contractors / third-party deprovisioning
- Contractors are provisioned via dedicated contractor groups with 90-day default access TTL and automated expiration. Deprovisioning triggers include SCIM disable events and HR offboarding webhook.

Next steps: Olga will follow up with the SCIM log sample and Karthik will add a short attestation paragraph for RBAC. Let us know if you want raw logs or a sanitized sample.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: saml-metadata.xml; scim-provisioning-logs-20250615.csv; rbac-role-mapping-202506.xlsx; mfa-policy-screenshot.png

Jamie, Markus —

Attaching a sanitized SCIM provisioning extract for tenant aurora-fin-staging (same format as our production export). The CSV columns include event_time, event_type, user_id, external_id, actor, source_ip, and change_summary. - SCIM error handling: retries with exponential backoff and a dead-letter queue for failing events; manual reconciliation jobs run daily.

If you'd like, I can export a 30-day delta (rather than a single-day sample).

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Jamie Park <jamie.park@aurorafin.com>, markus_klein@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-06-18T10:45:00Z
Subject: Re: AuroraFin SIG - RBAC attestation and least-privilege note

Hi Jamie —

Quick attestation on RBAC and least-privilege enforcement for the SIG:

- Role lifecycle: All role definitions are stored in a version-controlled roles repo. Creating a role requires a PR that includes: purpose, minimum required permissions, and an owner. The PR is reviewed by at least two engineers including one security reviewer.
- Automated checks: Our CI runs static checks against a least-privilege policy matrix; any role that grants wildcard or overly broad permissions is flagged and blocked until explicit justification is provided.
- Temporary elevation: We use time-limited elevation tokens (valid up to 4 hours) that are logged and require request metadata. Elevations are audited weekly and owners receive monthly attestation requests.
- Exceptions and compensating controls: Exceptions are rare and documented; for each exception we require a compensating control (e.g., IP restrictions, just-in-time session limits).

I'll paste a one-paragraph attestation you can include in the SIG response: 
"Redwood Inference enforces least-privilege through a PR-based role creation workflow, automated static checks that block overly broad permissions, and audited time-limited elevation for exceptional access. Role owners annually attest to access necessity and exceptions require documented compensating controls."

Happy to expand if you need a short diagram of the lifecycle.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Platform Access
Redwood Inference
